Subject: Security exhibit: staging access, evidence checkpoints, and pen-test definition

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time earlier. I attached the latest order form draft and our SOC 2 snapshot so you have them in one place (orderform_v3.pdf; SOC2-summary-2027.pdf). A couple of items from our side we want to confirm before legal starts final redlines: 

1) Pen-test notice window — your procurement note said 30 days. For MSA language our legal team typically asks for a 14–30 day notification for scheduled penetration tests and a 72‑hour notice for emergency/forensic access. Can you confirm Hippo Health’s preferred notice window?

2) Audit scope carveouts — we propose the standard carveouts for customer-provided data and ephemeral staging systems. We also want to flag that any sampling requests that require live user data need to go through an agreed SRA and a data minimization plan.

3) Staging access & allowlist — can you share the IP ranges and a preferred service account name so we can pre-provision ephemeral service accounts for the window?

4) Evidence cadence — to reduce churn we typically propose a short onboarding packet (SOC 2 PDF + architecture diagram) and then a weekly 30‑min evidence checkpoint during the orderform onboarding sprint. If that looks heavy we can switch to two checkpoints: kickoff + handback.

If you’re aligned I’ll loop in our legal (karthik) and security (jonas) with suggested clause language. If useful, we can do a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk the redlines.

Short signature:
Naomi Feldman

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the summary and attachments. A few quick clarifications from procurement/security at Hippo: 

- Pen-test notice: Our baseline is 30 days for scheduled tests; emergency tests are handled ad hoc but we require a 48–72 hour notice where possible. We can be flexible on the lower bound for scheduled tests if we get explicit windowing in the contract.

- Evidence sampling: We can provide a bounded set of logs and a staging snapshot; anything involving PHI or live patient data needs anonymization.

- Staging IPs: I don’t have the ranges handy today — procurement will follow up with a short spreadsheet (procurement_checklist.xlsx) listing networking contact and preferred maintenance windows.

- On cadence: weekly 30‑min checkpoints during onboarding sound fine. For long-term audit/renewal we prefer an annual evidence handback plus an escalation path for regressions.

Two asks: please have your legal propose the explicit MSA pen-test clause (notification + scope carveouts) so our legal team has something to redline against, and can you share the staging account name once provisioned?

I can do a 30‑min call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,
Emily Carter
Head of Procurement, Hippo Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-15T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit: staging access, evidence checkpoints, and pen-test definition

Naomi / team —

I reviewed the materials. Below are suggested redline language and negotiation positions we should take to keep the scope bounded while being responsive to Hippo’s requests. I’ll drop the formal tracked-redline in redlines_MSA_v2.docx but posting the core clauses here for quick reference.

1) Penetration testing / forensic access (suggested language):
"Customer may conduct penetration testing of the Services no more frequently than once per calendar quarter and with at least fourteen (14) days' prior written notice for scheduled tests. For emergency or incident-driven testing, Customer will provide as much notice as practicable, not less than seventy‑two (72) hours, and will coordinate with Provider's security on-scene contacts. Provider will not be required to provide access to environments containing live production data where doing so would violate Provider's data handling policies or applicable law."

Negotiation note: push for 14 days min and 30 preferred for scheduled; 72 hours for emergencies is reasonable. Resist open-ended language that allows ad hoc tests without notice.

2) Audit sample & data access carveouts (suggested language):
"Audit scope excludes Customer-owned production data and live patient records unless the parties execute a separate Data Access Agreement that details least-privilege access, anonymization, and SRA approvals. Provider will supply redacted/system-level logs and architecture diagrams sufficient to substantiate SOC 2 assertions without exposing live customer PII or PHI."

Negotiation note: require SRA + limited admin accounts for sampling; avoid full database dumps.

3) Evidence cadence & deliverables:
- Kickoff packet (within 5 business days of orderform execution): SOC 2 summary, system architecture diagram, list of retained logs, and contact list.
- Onboarding checkpoints: weekly 30‑minute syncs during the first 4 weeks; evidence handback at the end of onboarding.

Operational asks: we need Hippo’s staging IP ranges and a named service account (e.g., hippo-service-integ@hippohealth.com) to pre-provision access.

I recommend we send this language to Hippo as a suggested redline so their counsel has something concrete to react to. I’ll prepare the tracked changes and upload to the Drive.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Emily — and thanks Karthik for the language.

Emily: quick recap and proposed next steps so we can close the loop this week: 

- Pen-test notice: Redwood proposes the clause Karthik pasted below (14 days minimum; 30 preferred for scheduled; 72 hours for emergency). Please confirm Hippo is comfortable with that baseline or tell us the minimal notice Hippo needs for scheduling.

- Evidence cadence: we’ll do the weekly 30‑min onboarding checkpoints for the first 4 weeks and then an evidence handback at go‑live. For annual audits we’ll provide the SOC 2 package and agree an annual 60‑day window for any supplemental sampling requests.

- Staging access: once Hippo shares the IP ranges and the service account name we’ll pre-provision ephemeral accounts and generate an allowlist for the windows you request.

If that aligns, I’ll: (a) upload Karthik’s tracked redline to the Drive (link below), (b) send the suggested redline to Hippo counsel for review, and (c) book a 30‑minute call tomorrow at 2pm PT (unless you prefer another time).
